candidates.title: VIA-SD slim-verifier tier for speculative decoding

source_records.title: Exa/arXiv frontier AI scout shortlist
source_records.summary: Scout identified VIA-SD as a concrete DSpark/DeepSpec-adjacent speculative decoding candidate for Enoch Research Facility intake.

candidates.hypothesis: A three-tier speculative decoding verifier policy can improve local inference throughput by routing medium-confidence draft tokens through a slim verifier instead of forcing binary accept-or-full-recompute decisions.
candidates.mechanism: Use direct acceptance for high-confidence draft tokens, a slim verifier for moderate-confidence tokens, and full target-model verification only for uncertain tokens; approximate the slim verifier locally with layer skipping, early-exit logits, or a smaller same-family model.
candidates.description: Test whether VIA-SD's intra-model routing idea is practical for Enoch's GB10/local inference workloads and agentic prompt mix.
candidates.implementation: Review the VIA-SD paper/project page, build a small local proxy for slim verification, instrument accept/slim/full routing decisions, and compare against binary speculative decoding on fixed prompts.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Binary accept/full-verify speculative decoding or the current DSpark/DeepSpec static verifier path measured on the same prompts and backend.
candidates.success_threshold: Show a reproducible reduction in full-verifier calls or rejection rate with neutral-or-better output quality and a positive accepted-token/sec or latency result; otherwise produce bottleneck evidence falsifying slim-verifier usefulness.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if no practical local slim-verifier proxy can be implemented, if routing overhead exceeds saved verification time, or if medium-confidence routing degrades correctness on reasoning/coding prompts.
candidates.accessibility_delta: Improves home/local inference efficiency by extracting more throughput from existing model families without requiring a new trained drafter.
likely_failure_modes: slim verifier proxy is not equivalent to intra-model routing
routing overhead dominates
medium-confidence tokens are too rare on Enoch prompts
quality regressions appear before speed gains
candidates.novelty_comparison: Sharper than generic speculative decoding because the tested invariant is a three-tier verifier path for medium-confidence drafts, not merely draft length tuning.
candidates.risk_notes: Project-page code was marked coming soon during scout; start with proxy implementation or wait for released code.

candidates.title: Learning-to-Draft throughput controller for speculative decoding

source_records.title: Exa/arXiv frontier AI scout shortlist
source_records.summary: Scout identified Learning to Draft as a scheduler/control candidate for DSpark/DeepSpec follow-up.

candidates.hypothesis: Optimizing speculative decoding controllers for accepted tokens per draft-plus-verify wall-clock cycle will beat static depth/verification schedules on Enoch workloads.
candidates.mechanism: Model speculative decoding as a control problem over draft depth and verification size, using throughput reward rather than acceptance length alone; start with offline trace replay before full reinforcement learning.
candidates.description: Translate the Learning to Draft objective into a bounded Enoch experiment using recorded or generated speculative-decoding traces.
candidates.implementation: Review LTD, record draft/verify cycle traces, implement static, heuristic dynamic, and learned/offline controller baselines, then compare accepted tokens/sec and scheduler overhead.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Static Eagle3/DSpark-style draft depth and verification-size policy under identical prompt/backend conditions.
candidates.success_threshold: A trace-replay or live harness shows the learned/offline controller improves accepted tokens/sec or latency after accounting for controller overhead, or falsifies the controller with clear overhead/bottleneck data.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if trace collection is not possible, if controller decisions are unstable across prompt classes, or if scheduler compute dominates the speculative-decoding gain.
candidates.accessibility_delta: Improves local serving efficiency by learning cheap runtime policies instead of relying on expensive larger-model capacity.
required_evidence: static vs dynamic vs learned policy comparison
likely_failure_modes: accepted length proxy diverges from throughput
offline traces do not transfer to live serving
policy overfits prompt mix
runtime instrumentation changes performance
candidates.novelty_comparison: Distinct from prior DSpark scheduler idea because it operationalizes a throughput reward and controller-replay harness rather than only online heuristic scheduling.
candidates.risk_notes: Full RL may be too expensive; require a trace-replay/dry-run milestone before any long training run.

candidates.title: Early-token reasoning quality scorer for post-training data curation

source_records.title: Exa/arXiv frontier AI scout shortlist
source_records.summary: Scout identified early reasoning-token loss as a bridge between dataset quality scoring and post-training experiments.

candidates.hypothesis: The loss pattern of the first 100-1000 reasoning tokens can cheaply identify high-value reasoning traces for SFT, reducing curation cost while preserving or improving downstream reasoning performance.
candidates.mechanism: Evaluate early reasoning tokens with a small or perturbed checkpoint, use early loss/trajectory similarity as a difficulty/diversity proxy, then select examples before any expensive full-trace filtering.
candidates.description: Prototype a cheap early-token scorer for reasoning-trace datasets and compare it to random, diversity-only, and full-trace selectors.
candidates.implementation: Choose a small reasoning dataset, compute early-token loss curves with a local model, select subsets by score/difficulty bands, and run a tiny SFT or proxy evaluation against held-out reasoning tasks.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Random subset selection and simple embedding-diversity selection under the same dataset size and model budget.
candidates.success_threshold: Early-token selected data matches or beats random/diversity baselines on a held-out or proxy reasoning eval with substantially lower scoring token budget.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if early-token scores are not stable across seeds/checkpoints, if proxy evaluation cannot distinguish subsets, or if scoring cost approaches full-trace curation cost.
candidates.accessibility_delta: Makes local post-training cheaper by reducing the token budget needed to find useful reasoning data.
likely_failure_modes: early loss selects hard but unlearnable examples
scores are checkpoint-sensitive
tiny SFT signal is too noisy
reasoning traces have leakage or inconsistent formatting
candidates.novelty_comparison: Directly tests whether pre-training-trajectory early-token loss can become an Enoch dataset-quality metric rather than relying on LLM judge curation.
candidates.risk_notes: Must guard against leakage and distinguish useful difficulty from noisy/unlearnable traces.

candidates.title: Answer-divergence instruction data selection benchmark

source_records.title: Exa/arXiv frontier AI scout shortlist
source_records.summary: Scout identified ADG as the strongest runnable dataset-quality injection candidate because public code exists.

candidates.hypothesis: Instructions whose sampled answers occupy diverse multi-modal regions in embedding space are higher-value post-training examples than examples selected by one-reference quality or simple embedding diversity alone.
candidates.mechanism: Generate multiple high-temperature responses per instruction, embed responses, score dispersion magnitude plus shape anisotropy, then perform bin-wise selection to preserve semantic coverage.
candidates.description: Run or adapt the ADG pipeline as a concrete dataset-quality benchmark for Enoch's generalized-understanding scorer.
candidates.implementation: Clone/inspect WisdomShell/ADG, run scoring on two small instruction pools or fixtures, select subsets using ADG/random/embedding-diversity, and compare downstream proxy metrics.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: Random selection, simple instruction embedding diversity, and any existing one-reference quality score under the same sample budget.
candidates.success_threshold: ADG-selected subset outperforms or provides clearer coverage/failure evidence than baselines on at least one small reasoning, knowledge, or coding eval; otherwise produce a falsifying report.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if response generation cost is too high for the budget, if embeddings collapse to topical clusters only, or if ADG score does not correlate with proxy eval outcomes.
candidates.accessibility_delta: Gives local researchers a practical data-selection method that may reduce the amount of instruction data needed for useful fine-tuning.
required_evidence: ADG vs random vs embedding-diversity comparison
likely_failure_modes: answer divergence rewards ambiguity instead of learnability
multi-sample generation is too expensive
small fixture eval is underpowered
code assumptions do not fit local Qwen/Llama paths
candidates.novelty_comparison: More runnable than broad dataset-quality theory because ADG has public code and a specific answer-geometry metric to test.
candidates.risk_notes: Need anti-gaming checks: high answer divergence can indicate ambiguity, contradiction, or poor prompt design rather than high training value.

candidates.title: Auditable post-training curation ledger inspired by CuratorKIT

source_records.title: Exa/arXiv frontier AI scout shortlist
source_records.summary: Scout identified CuratorKIT-style provenance as infrastructure for Enoch dataset-quality and post-training experiments.

candidates.hypothesis: Enoch post-training experiments will be more reproducible and debuggable if every sample selection, rejection, hygiene check, synthetic generation step, and export decision is captured in an append-only curation ledger.
candidates.mechanism: Model each dataset item as a provenance chain with source, hygiene, quality-gate, hallucination/grounding, rejection reason, recovery, and export compatibility events before training.
candidates.description: Prototype a minimal Enoch curation ledger/schema and fixture pipeline inspired by CuratorKIT rather than relying on opaque one-off dataset filters.
candidates.implementation: Review CuratorKIT, define a small JSON/SQLite/Postgres fixture schema, run two dataset fixture slices through hygiene and quality gates, and produce structured rejection/export reports usable by ALI-208 scorers.
candidates.baseline_to_beat: A flat dataset manifest with only include/exclude flags and no per-sample provenance or rejection reason.
candidates.success_threshold: The prototype records deterministic per-sample provenance and rejection reasons for fixture data and can export a training-ready manifest consumed by a downstream scorer or dry-run trainer.
candidates.kill_condition: Stop if the schema becomes too broad for a small fixture, if gates cannot be made deterministic, or if the ledger does not improve reproducibility/debuggability of ALI-208/ALI-207 experiments.
candidates.accessibility_delta: Improves local training reliability by making dataset curation decisions auditable without requiring expensive external curation services.
likely_failure_modes: scope creep into a full data platform
quality gates are subjective rather than deterministic
ledger overhead exceeds value for small experiments
exports do not match training stack needs
candidates.novelty_comparison: Infrastructure candidate rather than a paper replication: it tests whether provenance-first curation improves Enoch's own dataset-quality workflow.
candidates.risk_notes: Keep v0 intentionally tiny; do not build a broad data platform before proving the ledger helps one downstream scorer.
